title: Short DAPT with Ticagrelor vs Standard DAPT in Chronic Coronary Syndrome Patients Undergoing PCI
official: A Randomized Controlled Study Evaluating Short-Term Dual Antiplatelet Therapy with Low-Dose Ticagrelor (60 mg) Followed by Monotherapy versus Standard-Duration Dual Antiplatelet Therapy with Clopidogrel in Patients with Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: the STELAR trial
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate the superiority of a short dual antiplatelet therapy strategy consisting of 1 month of DAPT with aspirin plus ticagrelor 60 mg followed by ticagrelor 60 mg monotherapy, compared with standard 6-month DAPT with aspirin and clopidogrel, in reducing net adverse clinical events (NACE) at 6 months in patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing PCI.
conditions: Chronic Coronary Syndrome in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)

interventions.name: Auretica 60 mg compresse rivestite con film

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥18 years
2. Acceptable bleeding risk profile: patients fulfilling ARC-HBR criteria may be included only if the treating physician deems a 6-month antiplatelet regimen to be safe.
3. No contraindications to study drugs, including aspirin, clopi-dogrel, or ticagrelor.
4. Diagnosis of chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) according to ESC guidelines.
5. Undergoing successful PCI with implantation of one or more new-generation drug-eluting stents (DES) or angioplasty with drug-coated balloon (DCB).
6. Indication for dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following PCI.
7. Willingness and ability to comply with all study procedures and follow-up assessments.
8. Signed informed consent after the PCI.
9. Creatinine clearance ≥30 mL/min, calculated using the Cockcroft-Gault formula.
10. Life expectancy greater than 1 year in the investigator’s judg-ment.
11. Hemodynamically stable at the time of randomization.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presentation with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), including STEMI, NSTEMI, or unstable angina within the previous 6 mon-ths.
2. Life expectancy <1 year due to non-cardiovascular comorbidi-ties (e.g., cancer, advanced renal failure).
3. Participation in another interventional clinical trial that may interfere with the outcomes of this study.
4. Severe anemia (hemoglobin <9 g/dL) not corrected before ran-domization.
5. Inability or unwillingness to provide informed consent or ad-here to study follow-up.
6. Prior stroke with residual neurological deficit or history of di-sabling stroke (mRS ≥3).
7. Planned staged PCI or revascularization procedure within 6 months after index PCI.
8. Requirement for long-term oral anticoagulation therapy, such as for atrial fibrillation, mechanical heart valves, or venous thromboembolism.
9. History of major bleeding (BARC Types 3b or 5), including gastrointestinal or intracranial bleeding, within the past 6 months.
10. Severe hepatic impairment, active liver disease, or transamina-ses >3× upper limit of normal.
11. Known platelet disorder, coagulopathy, or thrombocytopenia (<100,000/mm³).
12. Contraindication or hypersensitivity to aspirin, clopidogrel, or ticagrelor, or known drug interaction that precludes their use.
13. Ongoing active bleeding or high risk of bleeding that, in the opinion of the investigator, precludes DAPT.
14. Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or women of childbearing potential who are not using effective contraception.
